A_target.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]].
Then $T$ is [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] {{iff}} every family of [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed sets]] with the [[Definition:Finite Intersection Property|finite intersection property]] has non-empty intersection.

B_source.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]].
$T$ is [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] {{iff}} every [[Definition:Open Cover|open cover]] of $S$ has a [[Definition:Finite Subcover|finite subcover]].

substitutions.the open sets of the cover: the complements of the closed sets
substitutions.the covering condition: empty total intersection of the closed sets
substitutions.the finite subcover: a finite subfamily with empty intersection

validity_conditions: complementation must be an inclusion-reversing involution on subsets, which it is
the sets must be closed exactly when their complements are open, which is the definition of the topology
the equivalence is a contrapositive restatement, so it holds in every topological space with no extra hypotheses
proof_plan:
Let $\FF = \set {F_i: i \in I}$ be a family of closed sets.
Let $U_i = S \setminus F_i$, which are [[Definition:Open Set (Topology)|open]].

By [[De Morgan's Laws (Set Theory)|De Morgan's laws]]:
:$\displaystyle \bigcap_{i \mathop \in I} F_i = \O \iff \bigcup_{i \mathop \in I} U_i = S$
If $T$ is compact and $\displaystyle \bigcap \FF = \O$, then $\set {U_i}$ is an [[Definition:Open Cover|open cover]], so has a finite subcover $U_{i_1}, \ldots, U_{i_k}$.
Then $F_{i_1} \cap \cdots \cap F_{i_k} = \O$, so $\FF$ fails the [[Definition:Finite Intersection Property|finite intersection property]].
